title: Anomalous temperature dependence of polaron mobility in a nonlinear double-well potential: unbiased X-propagator approach
authors: Stefano Ragni, Osor S. Barišić, Naoto Nagaosa, Andrey S. Mishchenko
abstract: We develop an unbiased X-propagator method for calculating finite-temperature optical conductivity $σ(ω)$ and dc mobility $μ$ for arbitrary nonlinear electron-phonon interaction. We apply it to a polaron coupled to a double-well lattice potential, a minimal model for strongly anharmonic polar materials. At moderate coupling, the mobility exhibits three temperature regimes associated with confinement within one well, thermal competition with the barrier, and barrier-insensitive high-temperature dynamics. This sequence produces a concave temperature dependence of the mobility that is absent in conventional linear-coupling polaron models. At strong coupling, the mobility becomes nonmonotonic, and its temperature evolution is reflected in a characteristic redistribution of optical spectral weight. For parameters relevant to SrTiO$_3$, our results qualitatively reproduce both the anomalous concave mobility and the onset of violation of the Mott-Ioffe-Regel limit, thereby supporting nonlinear coupling to a soft anharmonic lattice mode as a microscopic mechanism for anomalous transport in dilute polar metals.
summary: The authors develop an advanced X-propagator method to study polaron mobility in materials modeled by a double-well potential. They demonstrate that this nonlinear coupling mechanism correctly predicts the anomalous concave temperature dependence of mobility observed in polar oxides like SrTiO3. This supports the idea that anharmonic lattice dynamics are key to understanding transport anomalies beyond simple linear models.
main_problem: To theoretically explain the anomalous temperature dependence of polaron mobility observed in dilute polar metals, such as SrTiO3.
main_result: The model successfully reproduces an anomalous concave temperature dependence for mobility and predicts spectral weight redistribution upon coupling to a nonlinear lattice potential.
method: Development and application of an unbiased X-propagator method to calculate finite-temperature optical conductivity and dc mobility for arbitrary electron-phonon interactions.
model_or_system: The system is modeled as a polaron coupled to a double-well lattice potential, which serves as a minimal model for strongly anharmonic polar materials relevant to oxides like SrTiO3.
key_observables: Static dc mobility (μ), optical conductivity $\sigma(\omega)$, and mean free path ($\lambda_{	ext{MFP}}$).
important_parameters: Coupling strength parameters ($g_2$), temperature regimes (low, moderate, high T), and the violation of the Mott-Ioffe-Regel limit.
main_assumptions: The use of a double-well potential to capture anharmonicity, and the extension of zero-temperature formalisms via the X-propagator method to finite temperatures.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $\mu$ vs. T showing three distinct regimes (confinement, barrier competition, high T), spectral weight redistribution in $\sigma(\omega)$ across these regimes, and comparisons between linear and nonlinear coupling models.
paper_structure: The paper develops the X-propagator method, applies it to the double-well model, analyzes the resulting temperature dependence of mobility ($\mu(T)$) across distinct physical regimes, and compares findings against experimental observations in SrTiO3.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical framework for understanding anomalous transport phenomena in polar materials by incorporating strong anharmonicity via nonlinear coupling terms, which is crucial for modeling soft modes in condensed matter systems.
